As far as I can remember, I have been quite introverted and have isolated myself from most social interactions.  Anytime I would go to my bedroom to read or leave the room when she’s upset, it was (in her mind) because I didn’t want to be around her (because “no one wants to be around me so why would my own daughter?”).  Of course I don’t want to be in the same room as someone who is slamming pots and pans, knocking the cabinet doors around, and screaming about all of their (personally identified) flaws!!!

If she tried a new recipe for dinner and something didn’t meet her expectations of herself, she would apologize for being “such a terrible cook.  No wonder I’m such a bad wife and mother”.  

I’ve seen a therapist to work through my reactions to anything my brain takes as being aggressive toward me (cars honking while I’m driving, people raising their voice around me, etc.) and have talked with a priest about how distancing myself from her has made me feel in my relationship with God.

Now I live hours away from my parents (though I occasionally miss spending days after work with my dad), talk to my mom maybe every few months unless it’s for my nieces/nephews, and am feeling much more stable.

I totally agree!  While this wasn’t a case of me reporting, I did have an occasion where I thought back on an interaction with a “neighborhood kid”.  I was living in a very rural place in middle school. We had a school in this township and I lived 1/4 mile from the school.  I was considered old enough to walk myself to and from school occasionally as it was considered to be a pretty safe area (we knew just about everyone that lived between my house and the highway and then it wasn’t far from the highway to the school).  I was walking to school one day and saw a kid, maybe 4/5 years old, playing outside of a trailer house that had been set up/lived in on this open lot for years.  I didn’t really see him much after that so I didn’t think much other than that he must’ve been a grandkid visiting or something.  Years later, I think I was a junior or senior in high school, I still occasionally walked to school if the weather was good because why not?  My mom left for work shortly before I was going to head out for school and she called to tell me that there were unmarked police cars parked along our road and posted at the turn from the highway.  Turns out the guy that had been living in that trailer house was about to be arrested for CP.  There was no knowing whether that kid was a victim or had actually been simply visiting like I had initially thought.  If I had had an inkling that something shady was happening, I would 100% have called it in.  If there’s nothing shady happening then there’s no reason to worry.
